title: Eighty-bit partial recovery conditional on a weak AES-256 related-key pair, BKN 2009 first step

target.description: The complete 14-round AES-256 encryption oracle is attacked, but this standalone first-step endpoint recovers only eight checkerboard bytes of K^0 and bytes K^1_(0,0), K^1_(0,2), totaling 80 bits. It is not full master-key recovery.

setting.key_relation: Fixed master-key XOR relation K and K XOR DeltaK from Appendix A. Five active key-schedule S-box transitions restrict the pair.
setting.key_population: A qualifying weak related-key pair of estimated incidence 2^-35; discovering such a pair is excluded from this conditional configuration.
setting.plaintext_model: Two 2^64 chosen-plaintext structures per repetition, varying eight checkerboard bytes and retaining the prescribed relation in the other bytes.
assumptions: The two secret related-key encryption oracles are already available and satisfy the weak key-schedule trail.
The source uses expected right-pair counts and random wrong-key voting; no numerical end-to-end recovery success is supplied.

time.note: Section4.2 first step: 2^31 repetitions of two structures of 2^64 texts. Sorting, candidate generation and ranking are included in the source dominant-order estimate; no exact full-AES conversion is supplied.

data.reported: 2^96 encryption queries across the selected pair
data.note: 2^31 * 2 * 2^64 = 2^96. The per-key Table1 shorthand is not multiplied by two a second time. No decryption is used by this first-step endpoint.

memory.note: Printed p.243 explicitly assigns 2^64 memory to this first step; the Table1/abstract 2^65 summary belongs to the completed recovery and is not substituted here. The storage unit and precise factor-two peak accounting remain unspecified.

preprocessing.note: No separately reusable preprocessing budget is reported for this first-step partial-recovery endpoint.

success.description: No numerical conditional80-bit first-stage recovery success is supplied. This endpoint is conditional on a qualifying weak pair; acquiring that pair is not included in its primary event. The first stage expects four right pairs,2^31 wrong pairs and2^47 random80-bit votes. Maximal voting does not supply a quantified80-bit output distribution. Expected counts are not converted into primary probabilities.

components.description: Section4.2 first step: remaining state-trail probability after the structured first two rounds, conditional on an actual qualifying key pair.

Section4.2: source assigns2^(64-93)=2^-29 to a structure producing a right pair. Retain this as its local first-moment approximation;2^31 repetitions give mean four, not an independently established end-to-end success distribution.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit. Local pair filters, conditional trails, weak-pair incidence and expected counts keep their own experiment; correlation is not a decision probability. Existing conflicts, resources, targets, settings and full-audit gates remain unchanged.

evidence.locator: PDF12–13 / printed pp.242–243, Section4.2 First step, numbered procedure and voting analysis.
evidence.interpretation: This is the explicit 80-bit endpoint before the source chosen-ciphertext or TA completion. Conditional scope removes only the outer scan over 2^35 candidate pairs.

limitations: This is an intermediate 80-bit endpoint, not complete recovery of the 256-bit master key.
Weak-pair discovery and subsequent key completion are outside this configuration.
Independent bounded S-box/linear-layer/exponent tests do not reproduce the full ranking attack or establish its global success probability.
